new_candidates.trigger: Public pressure over TECfusions' 'Keystone Connect' hyperscale data-center campus (up to 1,400 acres, potentially up to 3 gigawatts, at the former Alcoa/Arconic Technical Center); residents sought more transparency and regulation before further development.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23, ending 2026-11-02. Bars new data-center development but does not apply to TECfusions' existing Building J permits (already operational, delivering GPU capacity per an Aug. 27, 2026 company release) or to a land-development plan the township approved Aug. 5, 2026 for further work on that building. A new draft ordinance (H-1-style Heavy Industrial standards, noise/vibration studies, and a contested requirement that developers provide their own baseload power generation) was under Planning Commission review, with a meeting held Sept. 15, 2026. A land-use appeal (Protect PT and two New Kensington residents, filed in Westmoreland County Court of Common Pleas) argues the township improperly allowed TECfusions' expansion to proceed via permits and a land-development-plan approval without requiring a full zoning/special-exception process.
new_candidates.affected_projects: TECfusions' 'Keystone Connect' campus at the former Alcoa/Arconic Technical Center (up to 1,400 acres, potentially up to 3 GW); Building J is already operational and exempted from the moratorium, and a land-development plan for further work on that building was approved Aug. 5, 2026 despite the moratorium.
new_candidates.outcome: Upper Burrell Township Board of Supervisors adopted a 180-day moratorium/curative amendment on new data-center development (excluding already-permitted TECfusions work), to allow time to draft a data-center zoning ordinance; a land-use appeal challenging the township's handling of TECfusions' existing permits is pending in Westmoreland County court.

evidence.title: Upper Burrell data center faces new hurdles amid transparency backlash
evidence.supports: Confirms the May 2026 180-day moratorium, that it exempts existing TECfusions Building J permits, the Aug. 5, 2026 land-development-plan approval despite the moratorium, the pending land-use appeal, and the Nov. 2 end date.
evidence.quote: In May, the township established a 180-day moratorium on new data center development. The pause, however, does not apply to building permits the township already granted TECfusions for work related to Building J... The moratorium ends on Nov. 2.

evidence.title: Upper Burrell puts temporary pause on new data center developments
evidence.supports: Contemporaneous coverage of the 180-day moratorium's adoption, quoting township Supervisors Scott Brown and Ross Walker on its purpose and scope (new developments only, not existing TECfusions work).
evidence.quote: Upper Burrell has passed a 180-day moratorium on data center developments while it drafts an ordinance outlining conduct for future projects. It will not apply to existing work that data center developer TECfusions has been doing

new_candidates.notes: Exact adoption date not confirmed to the day; both sources describe it as adopted 'in May' 2026, consistent with the Nov. 2, 2026 end date implied by a 180-day term. No township-hosted resolution PDF was located in this pass.

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-05-06, Smithfield Township Board of Supervisors, adoption of Resolution No. 621 (Monroe County)
new_candidates.duration: Up to 180 days from May 6, 2026 (statutory ceiling Nov. 2, 2026) to adopt curative zoning amendments for data centers, data center accessory uses, and disaster recovery facilities; the process concluded early when the Board adopted the resulting curative amendment on 2026-08-12.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Resolution No. 621 (Smithfield Township), formally initiating the Municipalities Planning Code curative-amendment process; superseded by the curative amendment adopted 2026-08-12 establishing a new H-1 (Heavy Industrial) Zoning District for data centers, data center accessory uses, and disaster recovery facilities
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap: zoning ordinance did not specifically address data centers; adopted proactively to develop tailored standards and a dedicated zoning district.
new_candidates.current_status: Replaced as of 2026-08-12. Resolution No. 621 (adopted 2026-05-06) opened a 180-day curative-amendment window (statutory ceiling 2026-11-02); following an Aug. 12, 2026 public hearing, the Board of Supervisors adopted the resulting curative amendment early, creating a new H-1 (Heavy Industrial) Zoning District (carved from the southern portion of the existing M-1 Industrial District) as the only zone where data centers, data center accessory uses, and disaster recovery facilities may locate (as Conditional Uses); these uses are no longer permitted in the township's ED or M-1 districts. The Board said it will address additional concerns in a future amendment.
new_candidates.outcome: Smithfield Township Board of Supervisors adopted Resolution No. 621, opening a municipal curative-amendment window that it used to adopt (on 2026-08-12, ahead of the Nov. 2, 2026 deadline) a permanent zoning amendment confining data centers to a newly created H-1 Heavy Industrial District.

evidence.title: Data Center Curative Amendment
evidence.supports: Official township page confirming Resolution No. 621 (adopted May 6, 2026), the 180-day/Nov. 2, 2026 statutory ceiling, and the Aug. 12, 2026 adoption of the resulting curative amendment creating the H-1 Heavy Industrial District.
evidence.quote: Following a public hearing held during its regular business meeting on August 12, 2026, the Smithfield Township Board of Supervisors adopted the curative amendment addressing data centers, data center accessory uses, and disaster recovery facilities... The Board of Supervisors adopted Resolution No. 621, formally initiating the Municipalities Planning Code (MPC) curative amendment process for the Township's data center ordinance. Under Pennsylvania law, the Township has 180 days from May 6, 2026, to consider and adopt any amendments
